items.quote: We had also successfully completed a fundraise of almost INR114 crores through a preferential allotment sometime in the month of February 2024, which also enabled us to reduce the debt and build up working capital and need-based capex plans for increasing our growth plans going forward.

items.statement: Promoters converted redeemable preference shares to equity at INR55 per share in February 2024 preferential allotment

items.statement: 88 lakh preference shares remain outstanding with redemption extended to 2034-2035
items.quote: It's about 88 lakhs shares which are pending to be sort of redeemed and the maturity period has been extended till 2034 or 2035, I think.

items.statement: Viyash generated INR100 crores of free cash flow in H1 FY25 driven by working capital optimization and low capex
items.quote: And we also generated INR100 crores of free cash flow. I think this is a big achievement for this year, mainly driven by optimization in working capital and also low capex.

items.statement: SeQuent working capital increased modestly to INR425 million from INR4,201 million as of March 2024 to support growth in Turkey and Spain
items.quote: On the balance sheet, we saw a very modest increase in working capital, which rose to INR425 million, up from INR4,201 million as of 31st March '24.

items.statement: Completed INR400 crore QIP with marquee investors; proceeds to repay term debt and reduce net debt substantially in Q3 FY25
items.quote: we've completed successfully QIP offering. The same was a INR400 crores issue, which we successfully closed and have got some marquee investors on board.

items.statement: GSPL is a promoter entity in spun yarn; Ganesha supplies recycled fiber to GSPL and may exit its own spun yarn business later.
items.quote: So, we are selling the recycling fiber to the GSPL and we are making the yarn. And eventually, we may exit out of the spun yarn business later on.

items.statement: Warrant conversion due in May 2025 expected to bring in around INR 110 crores.
items.quote: So, the warrant conversion is due in May 2025, 6 months fr om now. So, around INR110 crores will come from the warrants

items.statement: Steady-state cash flow conversion from EBITDA expected at 60%-70% for new Odisha project.
items.quote: So, if you need the cash flow as Capex in our new projects, in Orissa so we are looking for about 60%-70% EBITDA margin will flow to the cash flow.

items.statement: Job work paid to Vishwa Rail is Rs 3.74 crore under a formal agreement for finishing work to deliver faster to railways.
items.quote: It is not 37 crores, it is 3.74 crores. Yes, we are already having a formal agreement and we are doing some work for the finishing side so that we're able to get the things done and delivery faster to the railway.

items.statement: Pre-tax operating cash flow was Rs. 78.18 crores in Q2 FY25, up from Rs. 75.29 crores in Q2 FY24 and Rs. 74.92 crores in Q1 FY25. H1 FY25 cash flow was Rs. 153.11 crores.
items.quote: Pre-tax operating cash flow was recorded at Rs. 78.18 crores for second quarter vis-a-vis Rs. 75.29 crores in Q2FY24 and Rs. 74.92 crores in Q1 FY25. Pre-tax operating cash flows for the H1FY24 was at Rs. 153.11 crores.

items.statement: IPO for automotive division is on hold due to market sentiment but may proceed later
items.quote: That is also ongoing, that is ongoing, but it all depends on the market sentiment. So as of now we have put that on hold, though we may go ahead with that.

items.statement: Generated Rs. 155 crores cash from operations in first half of the year
items.quote: In the first-half of the year, we generated about Rs. 155 crores in cash from operations.

items.statement: SEBI final order dropped insider trading allegations against promoters; penalty on accounting treatment stayed by SAT appeal
items.quote: we are glad to inform that the SEBI, the final order has come wherein they have removed all the allegations against the promoter sale of share. That has been dropped.

items.statement: Refundable deposit of ₹40 crore given for Mumbai hotel in Q1 FY25; ₹61 lakh deposit for Gurgaon hotel
items.quote: What we have done, in Mumbai, we have given a refundable deposit, okay? We are not spending the money, it's on lease. So we're not spending the money as such. So we have given only an ₹40 crore refundable deposit, which was given in the first quarter itself, okay?

items.statement: Monthly operating cost for Mumbai hotel estimated at ₹3 crore; ₹1-1.5 crore expected in March FY25
items.quote: Monthly costs will be around ₹3 crores. So in March, maybe ₹1 crores, ₹1.5 crores we might have to spend.

items.statement: Operating cash flow for Q2 FY25 was Rs. 442 crore.
items.quote: Operating Cash Flow for the quarter stood at Rs. 442 crore.

items.statement: Operating cash flow for H1 FY25 was Rs. 442 crore.
items.quote: For H1 FY '25, operating cash flow stood at Rs. 442 crores, underscoring our commitment to financial discipline and operational efficiency.

items.statement: Completed fund-raise of INR 218 crores via preferential allotment of equity shares and warrants; total fund-raise this year INR 342.55 crores.
items.quote: Additionally, we have completed a successful fund-raise of INR 218 crores through preferential allotment of equity shares and commodity warrants, bringing our total fund-raise this year to INR 342.55 crores.

items.statement: Promoter participated INR 45 crores in the fund-raise, of which INR 11.5 crores already paid; balance over next 18 months.
items.quote: And the promoter, myself, I've also participated up to a tune of INR 45 crores, out of which INR 12 crores – INR 11.5 crores or something approximately has already been paid to the company.

items.statement: Nomination and Remuneration Committee approved allotment of 25,052 equity shares under ESOP 2020; 110 employees included as of September 30.
items.quote: Recently, the Nomination and Remuneration Committee approved the allotment of 25,052 equity shares through the Fineotex Chemical Limited ESOP 2020, with 110 employees now included for ESOP as of September 30.

items.statement: Management focused on better payment terms, on-time collections, inventory and payables management, and profitability to improve cash flow.
items.quote: Regarding the better cash flow, there has been a lot of focus in terms of having better payment terms for the last, say, 1 year as we are evolving to improve our cash position. Our -- a lot of impetus on getting on-time collections.

items.statement: Free cash flow will be enormous after renovation completes; debt reduction strategy continues in Q3-Q4
items.quote: Once that happens, free cash flow will be enormous in Lemon Tree. I think we are sticking to our guidance that in the next 3 - 3.5 years, we should be debt free, but if we list Fleur before that then we will be debt free that much earlier.

items.statement: Free cash flow in Q3-Q4 will go mostly towards debt reduction, not renovation
items.quote: The free cash flow that we generate will not go towards renovation, it will go mostly towards debt reduction.

items.statement: Fleur Hotels IPO expected within next 2-3 years
items.quote: Well, I would reckon within the next 2-3 years at most.

items.quote: So, this was a personal matter because of which he had to resign. More than that, I cannot comment on this yet.

items.quote: That is just a typo, because last time it was repayment, I think, the format. So, this time, because of the transition of the CFO, probably these small things have happened.

items.quote: looking at the increase in the business and the scale to the tune of 15.5-odd percentage, there has been a similar increase in the receivables as such. items.quote: Mr. Srinivasan had to step down because of a conflict of interest. He has been appointed as a CEO of an insurance company as Operating CEO. With respect to Mr. Anil Chanana, he has also indicated to us his preoccupation and also his personal commitments.

items.statement: Positive operating cash flow of INR7.4 crores in H1 FY25 versus negative INR148 crores in H1 FY24
items.quote: We were able to have positive cash flow from operations of around INR7.4 crores compared to a negative or deficit of INR148 crores the same period last year.

items.statement: Receivables period increased mainly due to PSU customers; payables rose proportionally with higher direct costs and purchase volumes from scaling operations
items.quote: the major receivables are of the PSUs. And therefore, the receivable period has slightly gone up. And so far as the payables are concerned, they are in proportion to the increasing scale of operations

items.statement: ESOP cost was INR5.5 crore in Q1 FY25; reserve fell to INR4.45 crore in Q2 due to lower share price; last option exercise in March 2025, no ESOP cost in FY26 under current scheme
items.quote: There were 5.5 crores ESOP costs in Q1. And now, since the closing share prices were lower as compared to the Q1 closing prices, the ESOP reserve has come down to INR4.45 crores

items.quote: Based on the current ESOPs that have been given, the last option would be exercised in March'25. So, there will not be any ESOPs under the current scheme for FY 26

items.quote: receivable days have increased quite a bit around 70% or so half yearly to around INR41 crores

items.statement: Majority of receivables expected to be collected over next 4 to 6 months as clients normalize cash flows post-strike
items.quote: We do anticipate a majority of these collections to happen over the next 4 months to 6 months' time.

items.statement: Receivable days expected to improve substantially in FY26 as revenue mix shifts from outsourced to direct projects
items.quote: The minute as we progress and which we foresee, we are already doing that to direct work that improves our cash flow substantially.

items.statement: Chairman pledged 4.15% of shares for personal home loan, not for company CAPEX
items.quote: It was for my personal home loan. The loan was for my home that is why I have pledged it. Maybe it is for the time period of 2 years, 3 years.

items.statement: Trade receivables are around 96 crores with a turnaround time of 90-120 days
items.quote: So, what is our turn around for getting our payments because almost 90 crores to two quarters turnover and 96 crores pending payment - Ravindra Doshi: The turnaround time is normally 90-days to 120-days, because work is always in progress

items.quote: Yesterday, let me announce that this company has filed a DRHP for an IPO and the document has been uploaded on the SEBI website and it's also available on the website of Aegis-Vopak Terminals Limited. The capital raise in AVTL will help the company reduce a certain portion of the outstanding debt and also some portion helped fund other general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Management has no plans to increase equity base; promoters and Stanley hold 75%
items.quote: As of now, we have no plans right now. We do continue to basically look -- have you also understand, Stanley is also an equitable partner, and both promoters holding 75%. As of now, we basically have no plans.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free and funds expansions from internal accruals
items.quote: We are doing the majority of the expansions from the internal accruals and looking to the future thinking of the government, future policies of the government, we have designed.

items.statement: All warrants converted and allotted in last board meeting; promoter holding increased to 35-36% and management will look for opportunities to increase further
items.quote: Yes, we finished. We paid for the warrants, and it was allotted in the last board meeting. So, all warrants have been converted.

items.statement: Promoter holding currently around 35-36% after warrant conversion; management wants to increase further but needs capital to buy more shares
items.quote: We look for opportunities to increase it further. I need to also have capital to buy. The question of that as well.

items.quote: So basically, you will see these numbers are going to be decreasing in the next couple of quarter now. items.quote: Our gross debt as of 30th September and net debt is at about INR5,800-odd crores versus March position was about INR5,600-odd crores. So, we've seen a net debt increase of only INR200 crores in this current fiscal.

items.statement: Management will not raise equity via QIP in India due to low valuations; plans to list offshore subsidiary at higher multiples first
items.quote: We will not bring a QIP in India. Because India is not giving us the right value currencies. So, this was our idea. When we would talk to overseas investors, they were looking at enterprise valuation of 10x to 12x. In India, everyone gets 4x to 5x, sir.

items.statement: E&Y conducts internal process audit for all businesses and units; PwC assists with investor relations
items.quote: They do the internal process audit for all our businesses, all our units.

items.quote: So first of all, all these loans are for the net purpose of the associates and entities and all carries the rate of interest is not at a rate of interest or it's not free of cost.

items.statement: Bluebrahma and Sagar are ethanol group entities where the company invested equity and loans when taking over from erstwhile promoters as a group of investors
items.quote: So basically, Bluebrahma and Sagar are the ethanol group that we had invested. So this was our equity and loan contribution into that group when we had taken over those entities from the erstwhile promoters as a group of investors.

items.statement: Other income of INR47 million in Q2 FY25 mainly from interest income on idle funds given as loans at high single-digit rates
items.quote: Other income mainly includes your interest income. So that may vary from quarter-to-quarter. Some idle funds we are giving in the form of loan, which is high single-digit.

items.quote: the police has concluded their investigation and they filed a charge shee t against the accused in the court, stating that the account was opened without following the deal procedure, and it was done as a fraud against the

items.quote: NCLT rule is very clear that if there is already a pending dispute, you can't approach NCLT for it.

items.quote: As on date, the term loan outstanding is about Rs. 103 crores. India Ratings have reaffirmed the rating IND A and revised the outlook from 'Stable' to 'Positive' for Rs.500 crores bank loan. items.statement: No stake sale by management or previous management; any shareholder holding over 5% must disclose to exchange and company will inform exchange immediately
items.quote: No, see I can't say about what the shareholders will do, but I don't think so. If anything is there definitely we will inform you.

items.statement: New co-promoters Samara Capital and Convergent Finance acquired control; Cavitec Mauritius (promoter) stake to reduce from 51.8% to 33.5% post share issuance to Del Monte shareholders
items.quote: Cavitec Mauritius today is 51.8% shareholder, along with all other public shareholders being 48.2%. Post this pre-allotment, Cavitec Mauritius will continue to be the sole promoter, and will own 33.5% of ATFL, to be renamed Sundrop.

items.statement: ATFL will issue shares to acquire 100% of Del Monte India; Bharti Group to receive 21% and Del Monte 14% of ATFL equity
items.quote: What we will be doing at ATFL is to acquire 100% of the shares of Del Monte India, and in lieu of cash, we will be issuing shares of ATFL to the two shareholders of Del Monte Foods, and this will allow us to own 100% of the assets and business, including t he brand, of Del Monte India

items.statement: Del Monte acquisition structured as share swap with Bharti Group and Del Monte becoming non-promoter shareholders of ATFL
items.quote: Bharti will become 21% shareholder, as I mentioned, and Del Monte will be a 14% shareholder. They will be non-promoters.

items.statement: Del Monte H1 FY25 revenue topped INR300 crore with INR15 crore EBITDA (5% margin); Sundrop H1 FY25 revenue similar but EBITDA margin slightly down
items.quote: Del Monte, for the last year, FY24, was at INR542 crores of revenue, versus INR760 of revenue. items.statement: Company became zero-debt with cash surplus of ₹136 crores in H1 FY25
items.quote: Improved capacity utilization, working capital optimization and cost rationalization enabled us to become a zero -debt company and having cash surplus of ₹136 crores in H1 Financial Year 25.

items.statement: Consolidated fund position of Rs 592 crore retained for future growth and expansion, reduced from last quarter due to dividend payment, advance tax, and growth capex
items.quote: Fund position is also strong. There is Rs. 592 crore fund which is there which is retained for future growth as well as expansion . If we compare against last quarter , then there is a reduction because of the dividend payment which has taken place as well as the advance tax which you have p aid and the growth back CapEx which we have incurred.

items.statement: Collections for Q2 FY25 were INR182 crores.
items.quote: Collections for the quarter stood at INR182 crores.

items.statement: Estimated net cash surplus after completion of launched projects is INR1,277 crores.
items.quote: This results in a net surplus after completion of these projects. The cash flow will stand at INR1,277 crores.

items.quote: To support our growth ambitions and strengthen our portfolio, we have raised our fundraising limit to INR1,000 crores.

items.quote: We have had an enabling resolution of INR500 crores already approved and about INR1,000 crores updating has gone to the circular resolution. So that should be coming -- the circular resolution should be over by mid-December.

items.statement: Cash and liquid investments exceeded INR1,500 crores as of September 30, 2024, in addition to loans given as treasury investments.
items.quote: The company holds a strong liquidity with cash and liquid investments of more than INR1,500 crores as of September 30, 2024, which is in addition to the loans given as part of treasury investments.

items.statement: Normal credit period to distributors and dealers is 60 to 90 days but often exceeds 90 days; there are collection delays but no significant bad debts yet.
items.quote: Normal credit period extended is normally 90 days , 60 to 90 days depending on the customer profile. But it does go up beyond 90 days in most of the cases.

items.statement: There are delays with collections, but no significant bad debts from formulation business as yet.
items.quote: There are delays with collections, but we have not seen any significant bad debts from any of our formulation business as yet.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded by ICRA from Stable to positive outlook due to strong balance sheet
items.quote: We are pleased to share that our credit rating by ICRA has been upgraded, and we have moved from Stable to positive outlook, given the strong balance sheet.

items.statement: Standalone receivables increased due to higher precision engineering share with longer credit cycles
items.quote: Majorly, the reason here is, as the value of business in Precision Engineering is going up, and it is becoming the major chunk of the overall business. items.statement: KDDL committed to retaining majority stake in Ethos at 50.4% and does not foresee further stake sale
items.quote: KDDL is committed to retaining majority stake in Ethos. We are currently at about 50.4%. We do not foresee a further stake sale.

items.quote: There is an increase in the DSO days from 62 days in March 2024 to 65 days in September 2024. Clearly , there is seasonality. You can see that last year, from September 2023 to Q2 FY2024, it was 67 days, and it has come down to 62 days. So, we have no concerns about our receivables.

items.statement: Net cash and treasury surplus net of debt increased by Rs. 77 crores to Rs. 5,090 crores between March and September 2024

items.statement: Cash before Flipkart deal was around Rs. 550 crores, received Rs. 95 crores from deal, total around Rs. 675 crores
items.quote: The cash before Flipkart deal, it was around Rs. 550 crores and we got another Rs. 95 crores. So, Rs. 550 crores plus Rs. 95 crores is around Rs. 675 crores.

items.statement: Expect to have Rs. 550 crores cash after profitability of SastaSundar platform
items.quote: And still after the profitability of the SastaSundar platform, we will be having Rs. 550 crores, so you can say the treasury will be as it is

items.quote: this is without raising any additional capital. So, out of our own capital which we raised, we got around Rs. 96 crores funds from Flipkart deal, and out of some treasury income we have to add around Rs. 55 crores only.

items.statement: Interest cost and depreciation higher due to new plant and office expenses
items.quote: My interest cost and depreciation was obviously much higher than last year because on account of the expenses that we've made towards the new plant, the new office and everything, which is still to give you results, right?

items.statement: Preferential shares allotted in March remain unlisted due to regulatory conflict between paid-up capital exceeding Rs 325 crore threshold requiring main board migration and mandatory three-year SME board tenure; company filed SEBI waiver ap
items.quote: we had scouted for investments and once we got a confirmation from BSE, in terms of getting their in principle approval, that is the time that we had actually called for the money. So the money was called for, the shares were issued from our side as far as we are concerned and we had filed for PAS 3 also.

items.statement: Company filed waiver application under Regulation 300 on 24 October seeking relaxation of mandatory three-year SME board period to enable main board migration and listing of preferential shares.
items.quote: on 24th of October, we have filed for a waiver under regulation 300 that will give us a relaxation for this mandatory three year period. So we have asked SEBI to give us a waiver on that front, so that we can migrate early.

items.quote: the last, so to say the last limit for this entire issue would be that next year, September 15th, we are due to migrate organically. We will be completing the three year period for which is required and hence that will happen.

items.statement: Warrant money will be called on schedule with no change despite preferential share listing delay.

items.quote: The cash generated from business operations basically, what happened this time was that the operations that we have and the cost of producing goods was relatively lower.

items.statement: Plant delays caused higher in-house losses but lower cost of goods sold improved margins and cash generation
items.quote: So basically, the main reason for the cash generation was that the markets increased, our stock levels increased, our cash generation increased. But our plants were also delayed.

items.statement: Company planning preferential issue for garmenting and yarn manufacturing expansion, amount and mode not finalized
items.quote: It will be a preferential. So we haven't decided the mode -- the total mode yet, but we are mostly focused towards preferential.

items.statement: Bonus equity shares issued in 3:1 ratio, 3 new fully paid-up shares of Rs 10 each allotted for every existing share

items.statement: QIP proceeds used to pay off creditors from Rs 35 crore to Rs 10 crore and to buy raw material on immediate payment terms

items.statement: Inventory at Rs 133 crore, 60-70% is raw material including Rs 70 crore Hastelloy stock
